prompt: Check a table's schema before using it: find the required columns it is missing, and validate a table name. Complete both methods in SchemaValidator, then run the tests.
explanation: Databases fold column names to a single case, so a schema check has to compare with equalsIgnoreCase rather than equals -- but the report should echo back the spelling the caller asked for, which is why the required list drives the loop. isValidTableName is a whitelist: rather than hunting for bad characters, it accepts only letters, digits and underscore and rejects everything else, and a leading digit is banned because SQL identifiers may not start with one. Whitelisting an identifier this way is the standard defence when a table name has to be concatenated into SQL, since identifiers cannot be passed as ? parameters.
hints: For each required column, scan actual with equalsIgnoreCase; add it to the result only if no match was found.
A boolean found flag set inside the inner loop (with break) is the simplest way to express "not present anywhere".
isValidTableName: reject null and empty first, then Character.isDigit(name.charAt(0)), then loop checking Character.isLetterOrDigit(c) || c == '_'.
